run_params.method: Window-based escape rates from p2_5_age_stratified.json; no GMM re-run

full_pessimism.description: Overall block: all attritors allocated to R2/R6 starters who fail to escape (true worst case). Working-age block: attritors allocated at the working-age share of the analytical sample (not all attritors), reflecting that working-age R2/R6 starters are a subset of all R2/R6 starters.

partial_pessimism.description: Attritors allocated proportionally to R2/R6 status: overall block uses prop_r2r6_in_analytical = 27.3% (R2/R6 share in analytical sample); working_age block uses prop_wa_in_analytical = 7.9% (working-age R2/R6 share in analytical sample). See overall and working_age sub-keys.

rationale: Manski worst-case bounds assess the impact of permanent attrition on the escape-rate estimate. Under full pessimism, all 86131 permanent attritors (eligible but not in analytical sample) are assumed to have been R2/R6 starters who failed to escape. Under partial pessimism, attritors are allocated to R2/R6 in proportion to their prevalence in the analytical sample. Both bounds bracket the true escape rate; the observed 5.6% lies above both bounds. Attritors who cannot complete 10 waves are more likely to face persistent labour-market instability (consistent with R2/R6 membership), making the full-pessimism allocation the methodologically conservative worst case.
